people.role: Founder and head of Tầm Kiếm Đường (1162); the Tiêu son turned away from Lê Hoa Am's gate
people.appearance: A lean, sharp-faced man in a hunter's leathers, with a sword whose guard is filed with hundreds of small notches.
people.backstory: Tiêu Vấn Phong grew up on a story. His great-grandfather Tiêu Kiến Quang (tieu_kien_quang), a hunter of Hòe Âm, found a sealed cave on the mountain in 930 with a sword's cold light behind the seal, ran, and never found it again (A108). In 1150 the clan sent its first son, twelve years old, to the gate of Lê Hoa Am (A110). The family said it was for the nuns' learning. He went for the cave. The abbess Thái Lê Tuyết (thai_le_tuyet) looked at him, with the prioress Mạnh Tĩnh Chi (manh_tinh_chi) beside her, and sent him down the mountain for being a boy. He became a hunter and a guide. In 1162, at twenty-four, he founded Tầm Kiếm Đường for the men the hermitage will not take, to search for the sealed sword cave (V069). He learned the sword late, from the guest elder Sài Mộ Kiếm (sai_mo_kiem), and built the hall's canon with him. In thirty-eight years he has searched 412 caves and filed a notch for each in his sword's guard.
people.wants: To stand in front of the abbess with the sword from the cave and make her tell him to his face why she turned him away.
people.secret: He stopped believing he would find the cave twenty years ago. He keeps searching because the hall has no other reason to exist, and because he wants the abbess to have to refuse him once more.

people.role: Guest elder and sword teacher of the hall; the man Tư Không Hạc Niên beat in 1130
people.appearance: A tall, grey, beautifully dressed swordsman gone to seed, who drinks with his left hand so that his right stays steady.
people.backstory: A market son of Tống Khách Thị who was the finest loose sword in the north-east for a century. In 1130 he challenged the wandering sage Tư Không Hạc Niên (tu_khong_hac_nien) in his own market and lost in three passes. The sage handed his sword back and settled in the market to teach no one (A141). Sài left. In 1165 the young Tiêu Vấn Phong (tieu_van_phong) hired him to teach the hall, and he has stayed because the hunters ask better questions than duelists. He wants a second duel before one of them dies.

people.appearance: A cheerful, bow-legged mountain guide who carries a basket on his back in every season.
people.backstory: A woodcutter's son from Hàn Khê Thôn who hunted with Tiêu Vấn Phong (tieu_van_phong) as boys and founded the hall with him in 1162. He guides caravans and Pavilion envoys over the passes and knows every path on the massif. Thirty years ago he went up to the Gate Hermitage to ask about a cave and was turned away by the grey sister Hướng Thiết Lan (huong_thiet_lan). He goes back every spring with a basket of larch mushrooms, and she takes it.

people.role: A Pavilion outer disciple who failed the Frost Test three times
people.appearance: A stiff, careful man who still sits like a Băng Tâm disciple and hates that he does.
people.backstory: From the ice-hole village of the far north, he sat three solstice nights on Phiến Băng Hồ under Đỗ Sương Nhi (do_suong_nhi) and felt nothing but cold. He refused the Desert Pavilion and the vassals the Pavilion offered him, walked south, and found Tầm Kiếm in 1185. He teaches the outer gate here with the patience the Pavilion taught him. He is angry at it for teaching him that and nothing else.
